headline: High-risk shared-workspace automation: n8n can write/execute on the server while next-ai-draw-io uses MCP and broad network egress, creating default pathways for leakage, conflicts, and unverified cascades.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: n8n can read/write the server filesystem and execute workflow code, while next-ai-draw-io accepts natural-language commands and uses MCP plus browser/network access. If n8n passes document or file content into next-ai-draw-io, prompt-like instructions embedded in that content can steer downstream actions. The shared channel is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF n8n writes attacker-controlled text into a file that next-ai-draw-io later ingests, injection is plausible.
IF the two agents are connected through a shared workspace or MCP bridge, instruction hijacking risk increases.
mitigations: Add a manual review step before next-ai-draw-io consumes n8n-generated files.
Restrict n8n outputs to a dedicated folder with non-executable content.
Disable automatic tool execution on imported text where possible.
Use allowlisted templates for any n8n-to-draw.io handoff.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: n8n touches whatever workflow data it processes and stores secrets per-credential on its server; next-ai-draw-io sends content to external model APIs and supports broad network egress. If both are pointed at the same workspace or documents, sensitive workflow data can flow from n8n into third-party inference through next-ai-draw-io. The pairwise leak path is plausible in default deployments but not proven from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF n8n workflow inputs include secrets, customer data, or regulated documents, leakage impact increases.
IF next-ai-draw-io is configured to send those documents to hosted model APIs, data leaves the local boundary.
mitigations: Separate sensitive n8n workflows from any next-ai-draw-io input folder.
Use local-only models for next-ai-draw-io when processing sensitive files.
Rotate or redact secrets before exporting n8n outputs.
Restrict API credentials in n8n to least-privilege scopes.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP or content classification before handoff.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: n8n has server filesystem write and subprocess execution; next-ai-draw-io has browser, MCP, and broad network egress. If both operate on the same files or shared mutable workspace, they can overwrite each other's artifacts or race on diagram/document state. Because no locking or shared-state contract is documented between them, the conflict pathway is plausible and should be treated as medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or diagram file, last-writer-wins conflicts can occur.
IF n8n subprocesses modify files while next-ai-draw-io is editing them, corruption is possible.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories per agent.
Serialize writes with a simple file lock or queue.
Keep one agent read-only on shared artifacts.
Snapshot files before handing them between agents.
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency checks to the workflow.

D_cascading_error.rationale: n8n can orchestrate tools and execute commands, while next-ai-draw-io can act on natural-language commands and external model outputs. If n8n-generated content is treated as authoritative by next-ai-draw-io, errors can cascade into incorrect diagrams, API calls, or workflow actions. The default danger is elevated because n8n can trigger downstream automation and next-ai-draw-io can consume unverified inputs.
conditions: IF next-ai-draw-io uses n8n output as a source of truth without verification, cascaded mistakes are likely.
IF n8n workflows trigger actions based on those mistaken outputs, downstream harm can be irreversible.
mitigations: Require human approval before any action derived from n8n output.
Add validation rules for all n8n-to-draw.io payloads.
Compare generated diagrams against source documents before publishing.
Limit n8n to draft-only outputs for downstream consumption.
requires-engineering: implement schema validation and provenance checks.

E_compliance.rationale: n8n stores secrets on its server and processes whatever the workflow handles, while next-ai-draw-io can send documents to multiple third-party model providers. If regulated data such as EU PII or confidential business records enters both systems, residency and retention obligations may diverge. The profiles do not specify certifications or DPA coverage, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed by n8n and then forwarded to hosted model APIs, compliance obligations may be breached.
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the two systems, subject-rights handling can fail.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair unless policies are confirmed.
Use local models for regulated documents.
Document retention and deletion rules for both systems.
Restrict n8n credentials and logs to minimal necessary data.
requires-engineering: obtain DPA/certification review for each external API.
